best_for: Podcasters, teachers and home musicians who record and trim audio a few times a week and want a free editor that opens MP3, WAV and FLAC without a subscription.

points.title: Free, GPL and no paid edition
points.text: Audacity is licensed under the GNU GPL and the project says it will always be free. The only paid extra is more cloud storage on audio.com, which is optional.

points.title: Audacity 4 is a big change
points.text: Version 4 is a rebuilt app with a new look and a new .aup4 project format. The 4.0.2 notes say some features from 3.x are still missing and that 4.1 is meant to bring them back. If you rely on a 3.x tool, check before you upgrade.

points.title: Plugins differ by system
points.text: Audacity 4 runs VST3 and Nyquist plugins on every system, LV2 on Linux and Audio Unit plugins on macOS. Older formats such as LADSPA were not supported in the early Audacity 4 builds.

points.title: It sends little data
points.text: The FAQ says the app collects only what it needs for error reports and update checks. You do not need an account to edit; sign-in is only for cloud saving and sharing on audio.com.

points.title: Linux here is still on 3.7
points.text: The Flatpak listed here is version 3.7.8, published under the Muse Group name but not marked verified by Flathub. Audacity's own site offers 4.0.2 as x86-64 and Arm64 AppImages if you want version 4 on Linux.

points.title: Windows keeps the history
points.text: The Windows listing keeps 42 versions, with MSI installers for x64 and Arm64, so rolling back to a 3.x build is easy. macOS lists only 4.0.2 for Intel and Apple Silicon, macOS 13 or later, so downgrades there need another source.
